luke.23.p1.b1.text: Then the whole council rose and led Jesus away to Pilate.

luke.23.p1.b2.text: “We found this man subverting our nation,

luke.23.p1.b3.text: forbidding payment of taxes to Caesar,

luke.23.p1.b4.text: and proclaiming Himself to be Christ, a King.”

luke.23.p2.b1.text: “Are You the King of the Jews?”

luke.23.p2.b3.text: “I find no basis for a charge against this man.”

luke.23.p2.b4.text: “He stirs up the people all over Judea with His teaching. He began in Galilee and has come all the way here.”

luke.23.p3.b1.text: He asked if the man was a Galilean.

luke.23.p3.b2.text: And learning that Jesus was under Herod’s jurisdiction, he sent Him to Herod, who himself was in Jerusalem at that time.

luke.23.p3.b3.text: When Herod saw Jesus, he was greatly pleased. He had wanted to see Him for a long time, because he had heard about Him

luke.23.p3.b4.text: and was hoping to see Him perform a miracle.

luke.23.p4.b1.text: Herod questioned Jesus at great length, but He gave no answer.

luke.23.p4.b2.text: Meanwhile, the chief priests and scribes stood there, vehemently accusing Him.

luke.23.p4.b3.text: And even Herod and his soldiers ridiculed and mocked Him. Dressing Him in a fine robe, they sent Him back to Pilate.

luke.23.p4.b4.text: That day Herod and Pilate became friends; before this time they had been enemies.

luke.23.p5.b1.text: Then Pilate called together the chief priests, the rulers, and the people,

luke.23.p5.b2.text: I have examined Him here in your presence and found Him not guilty of your charges against Him.

luke.23.p5.b3.text: Neither has Herod, for he sent Him back to us. As you can see, He has done nothing deserving of death.

luke.23.p5.b4.text: Therefore I will punish Him and release Him.”

luke.23.p6.b1.text: “Away with this man! Release Barabbas to us!”

luke.23.p6.b2.text: (Barabbas had been imprisoned for an insurrection in the city, and for murder.)

luke.23.p6.b3.text: Wanting to release Jesus, Pilate addressed them again,

luke.23.p7.b1.text: “What evil has this man done? I have found in Him no offense worthy of death.

luke.23.p7.b2.text: But they were insistent, demanding with loud voices for Jesus to be crucified. And their clamor prevailed.

luke.23.p7.b3.text: So Pilate sentenced that their demand be met.

luke.23.p7.b4.text: As they had requested, he released the one imprisoned for insurrection and murder, and handed Jesus over to their will.

luke.23.p8.b1.text: As the soldiers led Him away,

luke.23.p8.b2.text: they seized Simon of Cyrene on his way in from the country,

luke.23.p8.b3.text: and put the cross on him

luke.23.p9.b1.text: A great number of people followed Him, including women who kept mourning and wailing for Him.

luke.23.p9.b2.text: “Daughters of Jerusalem, do not weep for Me, but weep for yourselves and for your children.

luke.23.p9.b3.text: For if men do these things while the tree is green, what will happen when it is dry?”

luke.23.p10.b1.text: Two others, who were criminals, were also led away to be executed with Jesus.

luke.23.p10.b2.text: When they came to the place called The Skull,

luke.23.p10.b3.text: they crucified Him there, along with the criminals, one on His right and the other on His left.

luke.23.p11.b2.text: “Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they are doing.”

luke.23.p11.b3.text: And they divided up His garments by casting lots.

luke.23.p12.b2.text: “He saved others; let Him save Himself if He is the Christ of God, the Chosen One.”

luke.23.p12.b3.text: “If You are the King of the Jews, … save Yourself!”

luke.23.p12.b4.text: Above Him was posted an inscription: THIS IS THE KING OF THE JEWS.

luke.23.p13.b1.text: “Are You not the Christ? … Save Yourself and us!”

luke.23.p13.b2.text: “Do you not even fear God, since you are under the same judgment?

luke.23.p13.b3.text: We are punished justly, … But this man has done nothing wrong.”

luke.23.p14.b1.text: “Jesus, remember me when You come into Your kingdom!”

luke.23.p14.b2.text: “Truly I tell you, today you will be with Me in Paradise.”

luke.23.p15.b1.text: It was now about the sixth hour, and darkness came over all the land until the ninth hour.

luke.23.p15.b3.text: and the veil of the temple was torn down the middle.

luke.23.p16.b1.text: “Did you not know that I had to be in My Father’s house?”

luke.23.p16.b2.text: “Father, into Your hands I commit My Spirit.”

luke.23.p16.b3.text: And when He had said this, He breathed His last.

luke.23.p17.b1.text: When the centurion saw what had happened, he gave glory to God, saying,

luke.23.p17.b3.text: And when all the people who had gathered for this spectacle saw what had happened, they returned home beating their breasts.

luke.23.p18.b1.text: But all those who knew Jesus, including the women who had followed Him from Galilee, stood at a distance watching these things.

luke.23.p19.b1.text: Now there was a Council member named Joseph, a good and righteous man,

luke.23.p19.b2.text: Who had not consented to their decision or action.

luke.23.p19.b3.text: He went to Pilate to ask for the body of Jesus.

luke.23.p19.b4.text: Then he took it down, wrapped it in a linen cloth, and placed it in a tomb cut into the rock, where no one had yet been laid.

luke.23.p20.b1.text: It was Preparation Day, and the Sabbath was beginning.

luke.23.p20.b2.text: The women who had come with Jesus from Galilee followed,

luke.23.p20.b3.text: and they saw the tomb and how His body was placed.

luke.23.p21.b1.text: Then they returned to prepare spices and perfumes.

luke.23.p21.b2.text: And they rested on the Sabbath, according to the commandment.
